label: prf:graded-markov-trace-from-gs-filtration
title: Proof of graded markov trace from gs filtration
html:
Proof sketch

The Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M is uniquely characterised by its cyclicity and Markov property (thm:jones-markov-trace). The GS filtration J^\bullet is two-sided [geckpfeiffer2000, mathas1999], so for T_1 \in J^a, T_2 \in J^b, T_1 T_2 \in J^{a+b}. Cyclicity then implies that \mathrm{tr}_M(T_1 T_2) - \mathrm{tr}_M(T_2 T_1) = 0 \in \mathbb{Q}(q)_{a + b}, which is the right-hand grading at the correct level. Hence the restriction of \mathrm{tr}_M to J^\ell descends to J^\ell / J^{\ell+1} (any T \in J^{\ell+1} has \mathrm{tr}_M(T) \in \mathbb{Q}(q)_{\ell+1}, which is strictly above the level \ell). Uniqueness follows from the universal property of the quotient.

The construction is purely algebraic — it makes no reference to analytic continuation, complex evaluation, or roots of unity. The companion block prop:residue-at-root supplies the algebraic definition of the residues required to assemble the GB-residue spectral sum (prop:gb-spectral-sequence).
